title: Haskell
subtitle: A pure, lazy, statically typed functional language whose ideas shaped a generation of programming languages, from a first program to professional practice.
description: Haskell is a general-purpose functional programming language, first defined in 1990 by a committee of researchers who wanted one shared, open, lazy functional language. Functions in Haskell are pure: given the same arguments they always return the same result and change nothing else, and effects such as printing or reading files are values of a special type that the runtime carries out. Its type system infers most types for you and catches whole classes of mistakes at compile time. Haskell is used for compilers and language tools, financial and blockchain systems, document converters such as Pandoc, static analysers such as ShellCheck, and a good deal of research; and its ideas (type classes, monads, algebraic data types, property-based testing) have travelled into Rust, Swift, Scala, Kotlin, C# and many more.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. No previous functional programming is assumed. It starts with installing GHC and running a first program, works through expressions, types, functions, lists and algebraic data types, explains type classes and monads concretely rather than abstractly, and ends with laziness and performance, concurrency and testing, the tools Haskell teams use every day, and a complete small project.

To run the code, install the toolchain with GHCup, the official installer, from [haskell.org/ghcup](https://www.haskell.org/ghcup/); it gives you the GHC compiler, the GHCi interactive environment and the Cabal build tool. Or try programs in the browser at the [Haskell Playground](https://play.haskell.org/). Every complete program in these lessons was run with GHC 9.14 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install GHC, run programs and explore in GHCi, and learn the core of the language: expressions and inferred types, functions, currying and pattern matching, and lists processed with recursion and folds.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Model data with algebraic data types and records, share behaviour across types with type classes, and write effectful programs with IO, do-notation, Maybe, Either and the Functor, Applicative and Monad classes.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Control laziness to write fast programs without space leaks, run code concurrently with threads, MVars and STM, test with properties, and build a complete project with the tools Haskell teams use every day.
